COMS W1007.title: Honors Introduction to Computer Science
COMS W1007.description: An honors introduction to abstraction, models and algorithms. Students design data structures and implement programs in Java.
COMS W1007.note: The archived honors course requires a score of 4 or 5 on AP Computer Science, or comparable experience. The current major and minor still list this course number. Check the available offering with CS Advising.

COMS W3251.description: Uses matrix operations and numerical examples to study linear systems, vector spaces, least squares, singular value decompositions and eigenvectors.

COMS W4701.pre: COMS W3134/COMS W3136/COMS W3137;STAT UN1201/STAT GU4001/IEOR E3658/MATH UN2015/STAT GU4203/MATH GU4155
COMS W4701.note: The Bulletin names three data structures alternatives and asks for any course in probability. The probability choices shown are examples. Python experience is recommended. AI minor students planning around COMS W2132 or IEOR E2000 should confirm data structures equivalency with the instructor.

COMS W4705.note: The Bulletin lists data structures and discusses Python experience. Probability, linear algebra and prior or concurrent AI or machine learning are recommended preparation. Only one of COMS W4705 and COMS BC3705 earns credit.

COMS W4706.note: Instructor permission is an alternative to the data structures prerequisite.

COMS W4710.pre: COMS W2132/COMS W3134/COMS W3136/COMS W3137/IEOR E2000
COMS W4710.note: Python proficiency and basic probability and statistics are expected. Previous machine learning exposure is recommended.

COMS W4721.description: A graduate-level introduction to supervised learning for data analysis, including principles of statistical learning and methods for building predictive models.
COMS W4721.note: The Data Science Institute specifies prior preparation in linear algebra, probability and statistics. The department lists no numbered prerequisite for the Spring 2026 section. Section access can depend on program and seat availability.

COMS W4726.note: The Bulletin expects the knowledge from an introductory machine learning course, plus Python programming. Equivalent prior learning is accepted.

COMS W4731.note: The course requires basic calculus, linear algebra and C programming. The Bulletin identifies no specific course numbers for this preparation.

COMS W4732.note: Also requires fundamentals of calculus, linear algebra and Python programming.

COMS W4733.pre: COMS W3134/COMS W3136/COMS W3137;COMS W3251/MATH UN2010/APMA E2101/APMA E3101/MATH UN2015;STAT UN1201/STAT GU4001/IEOR E3658/MATH UN2015
COMS W4733.note: Students should be proficient in Python or a comparable language.

COMS W4737.note: Sophomore-level preparation in CS, engineering or a related field is required. COMS E6737 is the graduate counterpart and carries overlapping credit.

COMS W4762.note: Requires proficiency in Python, R or Julia. An introductory machine learning course is recommended.

COMS W4771.note: The graph follows the current Bulletin. It lists these courses as examples of the expected mathematical and programming background. W3770 is recommended as a refresher. The linked instructor syllabus describes equivalent preparation for that section.

COMS W4772.note: The Bulletin also lists instructor permission and prior knowledge of linear algebra and introductory probability or statistics.

COMS W4773.description: Studies theoretical guarantees for learning algorithms, including statistical learning, boosting, optimization and concentration bounds.
COMS W4773.note: The W-numbered Bulletin record lists W4771. Daniel Hsu’s Fall 2026 section instead requires an advanced proof-based course and expects probability and linear algebra. For that section, prior machine learning is optional.

COMS W4774.note: The Bulletin also expects probability and statistics, linear algebra, multivariable calculus, and programming with algorithms.

COMS W4775.note: Expect to use discrete mathematics, calculus, statistics, experimental design and programming.

ELEN E4720.description: Studies supervised and unsupervised machine learning for signal and data analysis. Methods include regression, classification, clustering and sequential models.
ELEN E4720.note: Columbia Engineering’s course description specifies basic linear algebra and calculus, introductory probability and statistics, and programming experience.

COMS BC3160.note: Requires Calculus I or higher. This Barnard course overlaps with COMS W4160 for credit.

COMS BC3705.note: Equivalent data structures preparation is accepted. Background in probability or statistics and in linear algebra is also required. Python experience is strongly encouraged. This course overlaps with COMS W4705 for credit.
